message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"d56c1357eb360e35b67b40c020232b6d76965b0a9beb42c15a98be522abad18f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:85","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","units":[{"unit_id":"sec02-u01","module_id":"sec02-m01","objective_ids":["sec02-u01"],"title":{"text":"Who needs a Minnesota license","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Where your old license came from and how long ago it expired decide which tests you take and how fast you must switch.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F06"]},{"text":"Visitors and a few special vehicles follow their own rules, so knowing the exceptions keeps you legal.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-R11"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Priya, aged thirty, moves from Ontario, Canada with a valid license, and her friend Omar moves from Brazil with a valid Brazilian license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Newcomers from another state, certain territories or Canada with a valid license need only a vision test and an application, while newcomers from other countries take all three tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01"]},"result":{"text":"Priya takes only the vision test and applies; Omar takes the written, vision and road tests; both act within sixty days.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F07","sec02-F06"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: assuming any valid foreign license lets a newcomer skip the written and road tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"Only licenses from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada allow that; other countries require all three tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F07"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Canada or a state skips the tests; elsewhere takes all three; sixty days to switch.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A new resident who will drive commercially moved here this week. How long do they have to get a Minnesota license?","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F06"]},"answer":{"text":"Thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02"]},"rationale":{"text":"The newcomer deadline is sixty days for a regular license but only thirty days for a commercial one.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Who must hold a license","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid, unexpired license on public roads","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04"]},{"text":"Different paths for different drivers","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every driver on Minnesota public streets and highways needs a license that is valid and not expired. How you get that license depends on your history. A person who has never been licensed follows one path, a Minnesotan whose license lapsed follows another, and a newcomer follows a third that depends on where their old license came from. This unit sorts out those paths, the deadline newcomers face, the visitors who may drive on a home license, and the few machines that need no Minnesota license at all. Pay attention to the ages and day counts, because they are easy to mix up.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"First license or lapsed license","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Never licensed: written, vision, permit, road","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},{"text":"Expired one to five years: vision and written","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"If you have never held a license anywhere, you must pass a written test and a vision test, get an instruction permit, and then pass a road test. If you once held a Minnesota license and it expired more than one year but less than five years ago, the path is shorter: you must pass both the vision test and the written test, and only then apply for a new license. Notice the order in both cases. The tests come first and the application or road test follows. A lapsed Minnesotan does not get to skip the written test just because they drove here before.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Newcomers from states or Canada","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty-one or older with a valid license","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Vision test and application only","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Expired license adds tests","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"A new resident aged twenty-one or older who comes from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada and shows a valid, unexpired license gets a Minnesota license with only a vision test and an application. There is no written test and no road test. If that former license has expired, the picture changes. Expired less than one year means passing the written test. Expired more than one year means passing both the written and the road tests. Before the Minnesota license is issued, the newcomer must present every other driver's license and identification card they hold to DVS.","fact_ids":["sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Other countries test fully","fact_ids":["sec02-F07","sec02-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid foreign license is not enough","fact_ids":["sec02-F07","sec02-R01"]},{"text":"Written, vision and road tests","fact_ids":["sec02-F07","sec02-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. A newcomer from a country other than the U.S. or Canada may assume a valid license from home works the same way as one from Wisconsin or Ontario. It does not. A newcomer from any other country must pass the written, vision and road tests even with a valid license from the former country. The shortcut of a vision test and an application belongs only to newcomers from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada. When a question tells you where a driver moved from, check that first, because it decides whether the driver skips tests or takes all three.","fact_ids":["sec02-F07","sec02-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The newcomer deadline","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sixty days for a regular license","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-R02"]},{"text":"Thirty days for a commercial license","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Once you become a Minnesota resident, the clock starts. A new resident has sixty days to get a Minnesota license or permit. A commercial driver has a shorter window of thirty days. In other words, the commercial deadline is half the regular one. If you move here and plan to drive commercially, put the thirty-day date on your calendar the day you arrive. If you hold only a regular license, you have sixty days. These two numbers are a favorite pairing in practice questions, so practice saying which belongs to which until it is automatic.","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Visitors from elsewhere","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Nonresident fifteen or older, valid home license","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03"]},{"text":"No-license country: eighteen, ninety days a year","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Visitors follow different rules. A nonresident at least fifteen years old with a valid license from their home state or country may drive in Minnesota without a Minnesota license. There is also a narrow exception for nonresidents from a country that does not license drivers at all. Such a person must be at least eighteen and may drive a vehicle registered in that country for the current year in Minnesota for up to ninety days in a calendar year without a license or permit. So the visitor age is fifteen, but the no-license exception needs eighteen and has a ninety-day yearly cap.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the deadlines","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"New resident who drives commercially","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F06"]},{"text":"How many days?","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a new resident moved to Minnesota this week and will be driving commercially. How long do they have to get a Minnesota license? Recall the two deadlines. A new resident with a regular license has sixty days to get a Minnesota license or permit, while a commercial driver has thirty days. This person is a commercial driver, so the answer is thirty days. If the same person only needed a regular license, they would have sixty days. Keeping these two numbers apart is one of the easiest points to earn in this chapter, so lock them in now.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Who needs a license recap","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-R11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid license required on public roads","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-R11"]},{"text":"Newcomer rules by origin and expiry","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-R11"]},{"text":"No license for tractors, snowmobiles, rail","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-R11"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, everyone driving on Minnesota public roads needs a valid, unexpired license. First-timers pass written and vision tests, get a permit and pass a road test, and a license lapsed one to five years means passing vision and written tests again. Newcomers twenty-one or older from another state, certain territories or Canada with a valid license need only a vision test and an application, while those from other countries take all three tests, and every newcomer has sixty days, or thirty for commercial. Visitors may drive from fifteen on a valid home license, and farm tractors used temporarily, snowmobiles and rail equipment need no Minnesota license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-F10","sec02-R01","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-R11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u02","module_id":"sec02-m02","objective_ids":["sec02-u02"],"title":{"text":"Who cannot be licensed","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing the refusal grounds ahead of time saves you a wasted visit and shows which requirements cannot be skipped.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F14"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Jordan is seventeen, finished driver education, and has held an instruction permit for four months when he applies for a license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A license is refused to an applicant eighteen or younger who has held a permit for under six months.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"result":{"text":"Jordan waits until he has held the permit for six months before applying again.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking that reaching fifteen is all a teen needs to get a license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12"]},"correction":{"text":"Fifteen is only the age floor for a permit or license; teens also need driver education proof and enough permit holding time.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Fifteen to start, educated to qualify, six or three months to hold.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An applicant aged nineteen has held an instruction permit for three months. Does permit holding time block the license?","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"answer":{"text":"No; applicants nineteen or older need at least three months.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"rationale":{"text":"The six-month minimum applies to applicants eighteen or younger, and the three-month minimum applies from nineteen.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Reasons a license is refused","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Basic eligibility","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},{"text":"Age and permit time","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},{"text":"Withdrawn licenses and medical grounds","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Not everyone who applies walks away with a license. The manual lists clear reasons a license can be refused, and some of them have nothing to do with driving skill. In this unit you will see the basic eligibility rules, the age floor for permits and licenses, the driver education and permit holding requirements for young applicants, how a suspended, revoked or canceled license blocks a new one, and the medical and public safety grounds that the Commissioner of Public Safety may use. You will also learn the reporting duty that applies after certain medical diagnoses.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F15","sec02-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Basic eligibility rules","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Show proper identification","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},{"text":"Pass every required test","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},{"text":"Read signs and traffic laws","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Three basic rules come first. You cannot be licensed if you fail to show proper identification, if you fail any required test, or if you cannot read and understand official road signs or state traffic laws. In addition, no license or instruction permit is issued to anyone under fifteen years of age. And an applicant under eighteen who does not hold a valid license from another state cannot be licensed unless they present proof of completing an approved driver education course. These are gates, not suggestions, and each one must be cleared on its own before a license is issued.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Permit holding time","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Eighteen or younger: at least six months","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Nineteen or older: at least three months","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"A license is refused if you have not held an instruction permit long enough. For an applicant eighteen or younger, the minimum is six months of permit holding. For an applicant nineteen or older, the minimum is three months. Notice that the line is drawn at nineteen. An eighteen-year-old still needs six months, the same as a teen. This rule exists so that new drivers gain real experience with a supervisor before driving alone. When a question gives you an age and a number of months, compare them against these two minimums and you will have your answer.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Fifteen is only the start","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Age floor is not the finish line","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Teens need education and holding time","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a common error. Because no license or permit is issued under fifteen, some people think a fifteen-year-old can be fully licensed right away. Fifteen is only the floor. A teen also needs proof of an approved driver education course unless they hold a valid license from another state, and they must hold an instruction permit for at least six months. A license is refused to an applicant eighteen or younger with less than six months of permit time, so a fifteen-year-old who just got a permit is still months away from qualifying for a license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Withdrawals and medical grounds","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Suspended or revoked: reinstate first","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19"]},{"text":"Commissioner may refuse for safety","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19"]},{"text":"False medical information costs privileges","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19"]}],"narration":{"text":"A suspended or revoked license blocks a new license until every reinstatement requirement is met, and a canceled license also blocks issuance. The Commissioner of Public Safety may refuse a license for a physical or mental disability that prevents safe driving, or for good cause to believe your driving would harm public safety, and a court finding of mental incompetence can also block it. Giving false medical information on a permit or license application can cost you your driving privileges, and a medical condition may require a physician's statement on whether it affects safe driving.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check permit time","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Nineteen years old","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Permit held three months","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant who is nineteen has held an instruction permit for exactly three months. Does permit holding time stand in the way of the license? Use the two minimums. Applicants eighteen or younger need at least six months, and applicants nineteen or older need at least three months. This applicant is nineteen and has three months, which meets the minimum. So permit holding time does not block the license, although every other requirement, such as identification and passing the tests, still applies. An eighteen-year-old with the same three months would have to wait.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Refusal grounds recap","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19","sec02-F40"]},"lines":[{"text":"Identification, tests and reading","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19","sec02-F40"]},{"text":"Fifteen, education, holding time","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19","sec02-F40"]},{"text":"Report epilepsy within thirty days","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19","sec02-F40"]}],"narration":{"text":"To recap, a license is refused without proper identification, after a failed required test, or if you cannot read and understand road signs and traffic laws. Nobody under fifteen gets a permit or license, teens without another state's license need driver education proof, and permits must be held six months at eighteen or younger or three months at nineteen or older. Withdrawn licenses must be reinstated first, and the Commissioner may refuse for unsafe conditions. Finally, a permit or license holder newly diagnosed with epilepsy or a similar condition must send a physician's statement to DVS within thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R19","sec02-F40"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u03","module_id":"sec02-m03","objective_ids":["sec02-u03"],"title":{"text":"Proving who you are","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]},"why_how":[{"text":"DVS will not issue anything until your identity documents check out, and small details like a missing middle name can stop you.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R07","sec02-F19"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Lena's birth certificate shows her maiden name, but she now uses her married name after a marriage and a later court-ordered change.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-R12"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Mismatched names need certified proof of each legal name change, and every change in a series must be documented.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-R12"]},"result":{"text":"Lena brings her certified marriage certificate and the certified court order so the chain from her birth name to her current name is complete.","fact_ids":["sec02-R12"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: believing a clear photocopy of an identity document will do if the original is at home.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18"]},"correction":{"text":"DVS never accepts photocopies of identification, may refuse laminated or altered documents, and may confiscate fraudulent ones.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Full name, birth date, originals only, and paper for every name change.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R12"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A Minnesota driver's license without a photo expired eighteen months ago. Can it be used as identification for a standard card?","fact_ids":["sec02-R07","sec02-F19"]},"answer":{"text":"No; a card without a photo counts only up to one year after expiry.","fact_ids":["sec02-R07"]},"rationale":{"text":"A photo card counts up to five years after expiry, but a no-photo card only up to one year.","fact_ids":["sec02-R07","sec02-F19"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Identity comes first","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"What documents must show","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]},{"text":"What DVS refuses","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]},{"text":"Name changes and translations","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before any test or card, DVS has to be sure who you are. This unit explains what your identification must prove, which kinds of documents are refused, how an older Minnesota card can still serve as identification, what to bring if you do not have one, how to prove a name change, and what a translation of a foreign document must include. These rules apply to the written and road tests as well as to the card itself. Getting them right the first time is the easiest way to avoid a second trip to the office. Bring originals, not copies.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Name, birth date and originals","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R12"]},"lines":[{"text":"First, middle and last name","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R12"]},{"text":"Date of birth","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R12"]},{"text":"No photocopies, no altered papers","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R12"]}],"narration":{"text":"For the written and road tests, your identification must verify your first, middle and last name and your date of birth. If the names on your documents do not match, you need certified proof of each legal name change. DVS may refuse laminated or altered documents and never accepts photocopies of identification. It may also confiscate fraudulent documents. A legal name change through marriage, divorce or court order is proved with a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order naming the change, and if you changed your name more than once, every change in the series must be documented.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-R12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Old cards and two documents","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R07","sec02-R13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Photo card: up to five years expired","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R07","sec02-R13"]},{"text":"No photo: up to one year expired","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R07","sec02-R13"]},{"text":"Otherwise a primary and a secondary","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R07","sec02-R13"]}],"narration":{"text":"For a standard license or ID, you may show a Minnesota license, ID or permit that is current or expired no more than five years if it has a photo, or no more than one year if it has no photo. Without such a card, you present two documents, a primary and a secondary, and one of them must show your full name and date of birth. If a document is not in English, it needs a qualified English translation, and the translator must certify that it is full and accurate, that they are competent in both languages, that they are not related to the subject, and that a false translation carries a penalty.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-R07","sec02-R13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Photo versus no photo","fact_ids":["sec02-R07","sec02-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Photo card: five years","fact_ids":["sec02-R07","sec02-F19"]},{"text":"No-photo card: one year","fact_ids":["sec02-R07","sec02-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"Watch the two expiry limits closely. An old Minnesota card with a photo can serve as identification up to five years after it expires, but a card without a photo only up to one year after it expires. People often remember the five-year number and apply it to every card. If the card has no photo, the window is just one year. When a question describes an expired card, look for the word photo before you decide.
